# Part A: Basic Operations

## A1: Sequence Creation

```{r a1}
v <- seq(5, 50, by = 5)
v
length(v)
sum(v)
mean(v)
```

## A2: Vector Repetitions

```{r a2}
v <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), times = 4)
z <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), each = 4)
v
z
```

## A3: Arithmetic Computations

```{r a3}
17 %% 5       # Remainder of 17 divided by 5
17 %/% 5      # Integer division of 17 by 5
2^10          # 2 to the power of 10
sqrt(144)     # Square root of 144
round(pi, 3)  # Pi rounded to 3 decimal places
```

## A4: Vector Operations and Dot Product

```{r a4}
a <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)
b <- c(1, 3, 5, 7)

a + b
a * b
a > b
sum(a * b) # Dot product
```

## A5: String Formatting and Data Types

```{r a5}
# String creation
paste("Student", 1:3, sep = "-")

# Data types check
class(42)
class(42L)
class("42")
class(411)
class(TRUE)
```

# Part B: Data Frames and Conditional Statements

## B1: Create Initial Data Frame

```{r b1}
students <- data.frame(
  id = 1:8,
  name = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dana", "Elif", "Farid", "Grace", "Hiro"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  section = c("A", "B", "A", "C", "B", "C", "A", "B"),
  midterm = c(78, 85, 92, 67, 74, 88, 95, 59),
  final = c(82, 79, 96, 71, 80, 91, 93, 65),
  attendance = c(95, 88, 100, 72, 90, 85, 98, 60),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
students
```

## B2: Structure and Summary

```{r b2}
str(students)
dim(students)
colnames(students)
summary(students)
```

## B3: Calculate Student Average

```{r b3}
students$average <- round(rowMeans(students[, c("midterm", "final")]), 1)
students
```

## B4: Logical Column (Passed)

```{r b4}
students$passed <- students$average >= 72 & students$attendance >= 75
students
```

## B5: Standing Classification

```{r b5}
students$standing <- ifelse(students$average >= 90, "Honors",
                     ifelse(students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))
students
```

## B6: Custom Classification Function

```{r b6}
classify <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 85) {
    return("Distinction")
  } else if (score >= 70) {
    return("Merit")
  } else if (score >= 50) {
    return("Pass")
  } else {
    return("Fail")
  }
}

sapply(c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify)
```

# Part C: rbind() and cbind()

## C1: Append New Students

```{r c1}
new_students <- data.frame(
  id = c(9, 10),
  name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
  sex = c("F", "M"),
  section = c("C", "A"),
  midterm = c(81, 70),
  final = c(84, 68),
  attendance = c(92, 80),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Calculate derived columns to match original structure
new_students$average <- round(rowMeans(new_students[, c("midterm", "final")]), 1)
new_students$passed <- new_students$average >= 72 & new_students$attendance >= 75
new_students$standing <- ifelse(new_students$average >= 90, "Honors",
                         ifelse(new_students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))

students_all <- rbind(students, new_students)
students_all
```

## C2: Attach Quiz Vector

```{r c2}
quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)
students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz)
class(students_all)
students_all
```

## C3: Matrix with Column Means

```{r c3}
m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final)
m_with_mean <- rbind(m, mean = colMeans(m))
m_with_mean
```

## C4: Handling Mismatched Columns in rbind()

```{r c4}
# Same number of columns as `students`, but one column name is wrong
bad <- students[1, ]
names(bad)[names(bad) == "name"] <- "student_name"

tryCatch(
  rbind(students, bad),
  error = function(e) {
    message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  }
)
```

**Explanation:** `rbind()` requires the data frames being combined to have the same number of columns *and* matching column names. When the names differ (e.g., `student_name` vs `name`), R cannot match the columns and throws an error ("names do not match previous names"). If the number of columns differs, it fails with "numbers of columns of arguments do not match".

# Part D: Subsetting

## D1: Extract Name Column

```{r d1}
students_all$name
students_all[["name"]]
students_all[, "name"]
```

## D2: Extract Specific Rows and Columns

```{r d2}
students_all[2:5, c("name", "midterm", "final")]
```

## D3: Logical Subsetting (Attendance > 90)

```{r d3}
students_all[students_all$attendance > 90, ]
```

## D4: Conditional Subsetting with subset()

```{r d4}
subset(
  students_all,
  sex == "F" & (section == "A" | section == "C") & final >= 75,
  select = c("name", "section", "final")
)
```

## D5: Highest and Lowest Average

```{r d5}
# Highest average
students_all$name[which.max(students_all$average)]

# Lowest average
students_all$name[which.min(students_all$average)]
```

## D6: Sort by Average (Top 3)

```{r d6}
students_sorted <- students_all[order(-students_all$average), ]
head(students_sorted, 3)
```

# Part E: Basic Factors

## E1: Convert Factor Columns

```{r e1}
students_all$section <- factor(students_all$section)
students_all$sex <- factor(students_all$sex)

levels(students_all$section)
levels(students_all$sex)
```

## E2: Two-way Frequency Table

```{r e2}
table(students_all$sex, students_all$section)
```

## E3: Integer Representation of Factors

```{r e3}
as.integer(students_all$sex)
```

**Explanation:** Underneath the labels, R stores factor levels as integer codes that follow the alphabetical order of the levels (1 for "F" and 2 for "M").

## E4: Labeled Factor Creation

```{r e4}
sex_label <- factor(students_all$sex, levels = c("F", "M"), labels = c("Female", "Male"))
students_all$sex_label <- sex_label
levels(students_all$sex_label)
```

## E5: Summary and Group Means

```{r e5}
summary(students_all$sex_label)

# Mean average for Females
mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == "Female"])

# Mean average for Males
mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == "Male"])
```
